canonical_variable: Precipitation; Temperature; Hydrological Flow; Population Impact; Agricultural Impact
target_data_products: Medium-range forecast fields; ensemble forecast fields; precipitation accumulation; 2m min/max temperature; wind fields; EFI/SOT extreme indices; SEAS5 seasonal forecasts; Nino3.4/ENSO-style seasonal indicators where available
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, first target: precipitation accumulation, daily max/min temperature, EFI for heavy rainfall or heat/cold extremes, SEAS5 seasonal precipitation tercile probabilities, and any ECMWF-based impact-model inputs named in an EAP
access_notes: ECMWF has multiple access routes. The ECMWF Data Store API is relevant for CDS/ADS/CEMS data-store access; ECMWF Open Data provides a free rolling archive of selected real-time forecast products; older/archive access can involve ECMWF Web API or MARS depending on licence and dataset.
suggested_monty_use: Candidate cross-hazard forecast feed for rainfall, temperature, extreme forecast index, seasonal outlooks, and forecast-driven impact models
go_value: Supports common GO trigger fields across multiple hazards and countries
priority_rationale: Most frequent normalized source in the current corpus and appears across several canonical variables, making it the strongest first candidate for a reusable ingestion pattern
ingestion_notes: Do not treat ECMWF as one dataset. The ingestion design should map EAP trigger fields to specific ECMWF products and parameters. Keep EAP source fidelity visible; ECMWF should not automatically replace national agency sources.

target_data_products: Daily river discharge forecasts; probabilistic discharge; threshold exceedance; return-period layers; reporting-point hydrographs; seasonal streamflow outlooks; forecast precipitation inputs shown in GloFAS products
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, first target: river discharge forecast, return-period exceedance probability, flood probability at reporting points or basins, and seasonal streamflow outlook where drought/flood EAPs use it
access_notes: GloFAS forecast data can be accessed through WMS-T, tailored FTP on request, ECMWF MARS, and the Copernicus Early Warning Data Store. Some operational details require registration or request workflows.
suggested_monty_use: Candidate feed for river discharge, flood probability, return-period exceedance, basin or station-level flood monitoring
go_value: Supports flood trigger monitoring and return-period style thresholds in GO
priority_rationale: Repeated across several flood EAPs and maps cleanly to one canonical family, making the pipeline concept easier to operationalize
ingestion_notes: Harmonize GLOFAS, GLoFAS, and GloFAS labels. Station or basin matching will be the hard part, so GO should store gauge/station/basin identifiers separately from the source name.

dataset_or_source_family: Pakistan flood forecasting and river flow authority
target_data_products: River discharge; flood flows; gauge-station thresholds; cusecs values; forecast bulletins; observed or forecast flood levels depending on EAP wording
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target station-specific discharge and alert thresholds first, because the current corpus has detailed Pakistan-style riverine thresholds
access_url_or_api: To be confirmed from official national service or agreed IFRC/Pakistan data-sharing route
access_notes: No stable public API was verified in this pass. Treat as a country-specific integration candidate requiring source-owner confirmation.
suggested_monty_use: Country-specific hydrological feed for river discharge, cusecs thresholds, and gauge-station monitoring
go_value: High value for Pakistan-style riverine flood EAPs with detailed station thresholds
priority_rationale: High row count but concentrated in two documents, so it is operationally important but not a global first build
ingestion_notes: Requires country-specific integration and careful station/gauge metadata.

canonical_variable: Precipitation; Temperature; Wind; Hydrological Flow; Alert/Warning Status
target_data_products: Official rainfall forecasts; rainfall warning levels; heat/cold bulletins; wind warnings; tropical-storm alerts; river bulletins; national forecast products named in EAPs
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target the specific official product named in each EAP: rainfall amount, alert colour, storm signal, heat/cold bulletin, or hydrological warning. Do not collapse them into one generic met feed.
normalized_source_examples: DCCMS; DNMG; ICPAC; BMKG; INSIVUMEH; DMH; LMS; COPECO; IMN
access_url_or_api: Varies by agency; investigate per country or regional centre
access_notes: These services are essential for source fidelity, but access methods vary: public web bulletins, WMS/API endpoints, email/bulletin feeds, or data-sharing agreements.
suggested_monty_use: Source-family planning for official national or regional forecasts, rainfall warnings, heat/cold bulletins, wind alerts, and hydrological warnings
go_value: Preserves the official source named in each EAP and supports country-specific GO trigger review
priority_rationale: These sources appear across many documents and canonical variables, but each individual integration is likely country or region specific
ingestion_notes: Treat as an integration class rather than one pipeline. Build GO fields that capture agency, product name, alert level, issue time, validity period, and geography.

canonical_variable: Temperature; Wind; Alert/Warning Status; Population Impact
target_data_products: Storm track forecasts; wind speed forecasts; storm signal levels; official cyclone/typhoon warning bulletins; forecast impact areas; model-consensus products where stated
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target storm signal level, wind speed, probability/track cone where available, and official bulletin status. These are often categorical or mixed categorical-numeric triggers.
normalized_source_examples: PAGASA; RSMC Nadi; INAM; BMD; INSIVUMEH
access_url_or_api: Varies by agency; RSMC/NMHS products should be investigated per EAP geography
access_notes: Access may be through official bulletins or warning pages rather than clean APIs. Model-consensus triggers may require multiple feeds and explicit connector logic.
suggested_monty_use: Support storm signal levels, wind thresholds, official cyclone alerts, and impact-model triggers
go_value: Useful for GO because storm triggers often combine wind, alert status, probability, geography, and short lead time
priority_rationale: Strong design relevance and meaningful recurrence, but sources differ by region and hazard governance
ingestion_notes: Needs clear handling of categorical alert levels and N-of-M model-consensus rules.

dataset_or_source_family: Health surveillance and disease alert sources
target_data_products: Confirmed case counts; suspected case counts; outbreak declarations; weekly surveillance reports; district-level disease alerts; health bulletins
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target disease case count and official outbreak/alert status by admin unit and reporting week. National surveillance feeds should be prioritized over generic global dashboards when the EAP names a national source.
normalized_source_examples: EPHI; SRCS; ZRCS; NDCU; Ministry of Health
access_notes: WHO provides emergency dashboards and health data APIs, but EAP disease triggers often depend on national surveillance systems. WHO sources may be useful for context, not necessarily as the official trigger feed.
suggested_monty_use: Support cholera, dengue, AWD, and official disease-alert triggers using case counts or health bulletins
go_value: Helps GO represent disease triggers that are not forecast-model based
priority_rationale: Important for public health EAPs, but data availability and update frequency are likely country-specific
ingestion_notes: Expect manual or semi-automated ingestion before full API integration. Preserve district/week reporting metadata and source authority.

canonical_variable: Agricultural Impact; Precipitation; Population Impact; Other
dataset_or_source_family: Food security and drought impact sources
target_data_products: Food insecurity projections; IPC/CH phase classifications; FEWS NET projection products; rainfall/seasonal context products; livestock or pasture indicators where named
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target food insecurity phase/projection by admin unit, IPC/CH classification, and FEWS NET projection indicators used directly as thresholds
normalized_source_examples: FEWSNET; FEWSnet; Cadre Harmonise; Ministry of Livestock
access_notes: FEWS NET provides an FDW REST API with public and authenticated access patterns. IPC/CH API access requires requesting an API key and documentation from IPC.
suggested_monty_use: Support drought, food insecurity, livestock, IPC/Cadre-style, and seasonal impact triggers
go_value: Connects trigger thresholds to slower-onset anticipatory-action decisions in GO
priority_rationale: Lower frequency than ECMWF/GloFAS, but strategically important for drought and food-security actions
ingestion_notes: Harmonize FEWSNET and FEWSnet. These products are often monthly/seasonal projections or assessments rather than daily polling feeds.

target_data_products: Affected-population estimates; exposure layers; population movement indicators; operational capacity indicators; humanitarian baseline datasets; GO operational references
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target affected-population counts, exposed population, admin-unit baselines, and operational-capacity indicators only when they are explicit trigger conditions
normalized_source_examples: OCHA; NOA; IFRC; IFRC GO Platform; Steering Committee of the Migration Roundtable
access_notes: HDX has a CKAN API for dataset discovery/metadata and HAPI for standardized humanitarian indicators. It may not provide every EAP-specific operational indicator directly.
suggested_monty_use: Support affected-population, movement, exposure, and operational-capacity triggers
go_value: Useful for representing non-meteorological decision criteria in GO
priority_rationale: Important for triggers where hazard data alone is not sufficient, but less suited to automated threshold monitoring
ingestion_notes: Likely requires manual validation and links to existing GO/HDX-style data rather than simple forecast ingestion.

target_data_products: CHIRPS rainfall estimates; CHIRPS v3 rainfall history; CHIRPS-GEFS 5-day, 10-day, and 15-day bias-corrected rainfall forecasts; rainfall anomalies
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target CHIRPS rainfall history for context/verification and CHIRPS-GEFS rainfall forecasts for rainfall amount/anomaly triggers where a compatible forecast source is acceptable
normalized_source_examples: Not prominent in normalized source field; included as recommended supporting rainfall family
access_notes: CHIRPS is a rainfall dataset and CHIRPS-GEFS provides bias-corrected forecast rainfall products. Use as supporting candidate, not as evidence that the current corpus explicitly names CHIRPS.
suggested_monty_use: Support rainfall accumulation, anomaly, and drought/rainfall verification workflows
go_value: Adds a practical rainfall data family for Monty even where EAP text names broader rainfall monitoring rather than an API-ready source
priority_rationale: Not counted in the current normalized source evidence, but recommended in the GO integration plan as a plausible rainfall ingestion family
ingestion_notes: Clearly label as a recommended supporting source rather than a source observed frequently in this corpus.

target_data_products: Ignition probability; fire danger rating; wind; humidity; wildfire spread or monitoring bulletins
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target ignition probability and official fire-danger alert level only where an EAP explicitly names them
access_url_or_api: To be confirmed from official national fire authority or Copernicus/EFFIS-style source where relevant
access_notes: No stable source API was verified for the specific corpus source in this pass. CEMS wildfire/EFFIS may be investigated separately if wildfire triggers expand.
suggested_monty_use: Represent wildfire risk, ignition probability, wind, and humidity conditions where they appear in EAPs
go_value: Keeps less common hazards structurally representable in GO
priority_rationale: Low frequency in current corpus and likely requires specialist national data
ingestion_notes: Keep in taxonomy and review workflow, but not a first ingestion priority.

target_data_products: Volcanic alert level; ash deposition; seismic/monitoring parameters; observatory bulletins
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target official volcanic alert level and ash-deposition thresholds where explicitly stated
access_url_or_api: To be confirmed from official national observatory source
access_notes: Often bulletin-based and country-specific. A general API should not be assumed without source-owner confirmation.
suggested_monty_use: Represent ash deposition, seismic monitoring, and volcanic alert levels
go_value: Supports specialized volcanic EAP ingestion without forcing volcanic alerts into weather fields
priority_rationale: Specialized and low frequency in the current corpus
ingestion_notes: Likely country-specific and alert-bulletin based. Treat as structured manual ingestion first.

target_data_products: Response capacity; institutional readiness; migration movement; operational criteria; non-standard humanitarian decision indicators
priority_data_products_for_go: For GO, target structured manual capture first: source name, indicator name, threshold, geography, and update frequency
normalized_source_examples: Steering Committee of the Migration Roundtable; IFRC operational references
access_url_or_api: No single API; source-specific review required
access_notes: These are legitimate trigger inputs but unlikely to map to one reusable data pipeline.
suggested_monty_use: Represent non-standard triggers such as migration, response capacity, or institutional criteria
go_value: Prevents unusual but legitimate EAP logic from being lost
priority_rationale: Low frequency and less suitable for centralized automated monitoring
ingestion_notes: Keep as reviewable structured fields and notes rather than near-term automated ingestion.
